title: Resisting Harmful Instructions through Training-Free Weight Editing
abstract: arXiv:2610.21189v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Instruction-following language models can comply with requests that conflict with intended behaviors and safety alignment. We introduce a training-free weight-editing approach for reducing compliance with targeted undesirable instructions. Our method needs only forward passes on a small set of prompt pairs per target behavior, and because the edit is stored in the model's weights, changing or deleting instructions in the prompt cannot undo the weight modification. We evaluate the approach on two target harmful behaviors across five instruction-tuned models: instructed falsehood and instructed sexism. On two instructed-lying benchmarks, it improves mean honest response rates by 6.2 and 4.6 percentage points over the strongest alternative, significantly on three of the five models and within noise on the other two. In a controlled study of seven prompt formats, it maintains higher honest-response rates than single-layer activation steering

translated_title: 通过无需训练的权重编辑抵抗有害指令
translated_abstract: 遵循指令的语言模型可能会服从与预期行为和安全对齐相冲突的请求。我们提出了一种无需训练的权重编辑方法，用于减少模型对特定不良指令的服从。该方法只需针对每个目标行为在少量提示对上执行前向传播，并且由于编辑结果存储在模型的权重中，因此改变或删除提示中的指令也无法撤销权重修改。我们在五个指令微调模型上针对两种目标有害行为（指令性谎言和指令性性别歧视）评估了该方法。在两个指令性谎言基准测试中，与最强的替代方法相比，该方法将平均诚实回答率分别提高了6.2和4.6个百分点，在五个模型中的三个上提升显著，另外两个模型的差异在噪声范围内。在涵盖七种提示格式的对照研究中，该方法比单层激活引导方法保持了更高的诚实回答率。
tldr: 本文提出一种无需训练的权重编辑方法，仅需在少量提示对上执行前向传播即可修改模型权重，使模型抵抗指令性谎言和性别歧视等有害指令，且这种防御无法通过修改提示来绕过。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a training-free weight editing approach that requires only forward passes on a small set of prompt pairs to modify model weights, enabling models to resist harmful instructions like instructed falsehood and sexism in a way that cannot be undone by changing prompts.
